messages:
Maya Nguyen: Quick sync — found ~3.2k near-duplicate prompts in the open-domain dev/train split after the latest harvest. Need a small dedupe + golden refresh before we run the 4-bit quant smoke.

Raj Patel: Where are the duplicates mostly coming from? buckets / time ranges?

Maya Nguyen: Mostly `user-sim` and `web-scrape-2025-09`. I ran a fast fingerprint clusterer (simhash). Sample cluster sizes: 1. 1200 singletons, 2. ~900 size-2, 3. 150 size 3-8, rest are long tails.

Maya Nguyen: Quick pipeline I used:
```
# cluster by fingerprint (fast pass)
python tools/cluster_prompts.py \  --input s3://redwood-datasets/open-dev-2026.jsonl \  --fingerprint simhash \  --threshold 0.9 \  --output s3://redwood-datasets/clustered/open-dev-clusters-1791234567.jsonl
```

labeler-bot: Assigned 150 clusters to @Olivia Chen for manual inspection. ETA 48h. :clipboard:

Olivia Chen: Taking the batch. Quick note — I'll skip clusters with >20 near-variants and escalate those to Sam (they look like dataset-level duplicates).

Sam Torres: We should canonicalize, not delete. Plan: choose a canonical prompt per cluster, keep mapping in `dedupe_map.jsonl`, and remove duplicates from the golden/dev shards. Also re-run evals to measure leakage impact.

Ana Li: FYI the latest quant-compile (v2-quant4) shows a slight ORACLE drop on intent detection in our current golden (pre-dedupe) — ~1.8%. That might be from leakage; dedupe could change the numbers both ways.

Frank Gomez: Proposed workflow: 1) labeler pass & canonicalize mapping 2) update golden set (remove duped entries + add prioritized canonicals) 3) run full eval-suite (intent, slots, rouge-like, safety checks) 4) if regression >1% on core metrics, rollback quant and investigate.

Maya Nguyen: Priority for this thread: 1) finish manual canonicalization, 2) generate new golden file + provenance, 3) run evals with `eval-suite` and compare.

Raj Patel: I'll add a quick pipeline check to detect near-duplicates during model onboarding so future leaks are flagged earlier. Short-term manual patch, long-term automation.

Olivia Chen: Question on labeling schema — do we mark cluster members as `merge->canonical_id` or as `canonicalize` with a chosen preferred prompt id? I prefer storing mapping like `{dupe_id: canonical_id}` so we can reverse if needed.

Sam Torres: Agreed — mapping approach. Also update `docs/dataset/golden_policy.md` with the canonicalization rule.

Olivia Chen: :white_check_mark: Starting labeling now. I'll push `clusters-prioritized-1791234567.jsonl` to the labeling queue and tag Sam on big clusters. ETA ~36h.

Maya Nguyen: CI hook to run after labeling:
```
# run evals on new golden set
./eval/run_on_golden.sh --model v2-quant4 --prompts s3://redwood-datasets/golden/open-dev-golden-1791234567.jsonl --metrics intent,slot,quality --output evals/1791234567/
```

ci-bot: CI triggered: eval job #4823 started for branch `dedupe/golden-1791234567` — logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/4823

Frank Gomez: If evals show >1% regression on any core metric, halt the rollout and open a regression issue linking eval diffs + sample failing prompts. Otherwise, proceed with quant smoke and monitor.

Maya Nguyen: Sounds good. I'll own release gating for this window. Thanks everyone — ping here if you see any clusters that need policy escalation. :eyes:
